title: dense-performance-evidence
summary: Taxonomy of performance evidence an optimization agent needs, ordered by collection cost and diagnostic power. Maps evidence types to the questions they answer and the claims they can support. Use to decide which evidence to collect next, avoid over-claiming from cheap evidence, and structure a measurement campaign.

skill_metadata.name: dense-performance-evidence
skill_metadata.description: Taxonomy of performance evidence an optimization agent needs, ordered by collection cost and diagnostic power. Maps evidence types to the questions they answer and the claims they can support. Use to decide which evidence to collect next, avoid over-claiming from cheap evidence, and structure a measurement campaign.

applicability.scope: Deciding which performance evidence to collect next and which claim each evidence level supports, from correctness through microbenchmark, component profile, isolated scenario benchmark and multi-regime serving benchmark to a production A/B experiment; also structuring a measurement campaign
applicability.prerequisites: Level 0 correctness evidence is collected before any performance measurement; a Level 5 experiment needs production infrastructure, traffic splitting and statistical power
applicability.input_contract: The claim to be made or the question to answer, and the evidence already collected with its level, workload, hardware/software context and controls
applicability.produced_artifact: The minimum evidence level each claim requires, the next evidence to collect under the escalation rule, and negative-result records with hypothesis, evidence level, the metric that did not improve, context and the reason if known; a classification of evidence, not a measurement
failure_modes: An md5 match or a test pass is read as semantically correct output or as support for a performance claim
A microbenchmark improvement is reported as an inference throughput gain
Absolute kernel durations or single collective latencies are compared across devices or sessions
A win on one fixed workload or concurrency is generalized to production traffic
Worse metrics, per-task regressions or negative results are discarded, or a shared task budget is taken as equal total cost
applicability.refusal_point: Withholds any claim above the level its evidence reaches, leaves an unresolved source protocol or denominator mismatch unresolved, and lets neither upstream scores nor local packaging checks promote an InferRSI candidate

recommendations: Collect Level 0 first and profile at Level 2 before implementing; escalate to Level 3 only after a promising Level 2 result, and to Level 4 only after a Level 3 win worth validating across regimes.
Collect a Level 1 microbenchmark only for an isolated-kernel question after Level 2 has confirmed that kernel is on the critical path.

For a Level 1 claim, pin input shape and dtype, exclude warmup, synchronize before timing, run at least 10 repetitions and report median and IQR; for a Level 3 claim, match hardware, software stack, model revision and inputs, run at least 3 repetitions and alternate A/B/A order.
Read the admission/drain occupancy case when interpreting finite service cohorts; phase-selected occupancy is not end-to-end gain.
limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
Original typed source inventory is not normalized; retain source identities and limits in the procedure/readsets.
